research.name: Research
research.desc: Nail the facts first; every claim sourced

goal.office:
Turn {source} into {output} for {audience}.
Keep every fact and number from the original; mark anything uncertain as TBC; length: {length}; due: {deadline}.
Do not modify the original files under {source} — write the result to a new file.
goal.dev:
Do {task} in {repo}.
Limits: keep changes within {scope}; do not touch {forbidden}; done means "{verify}" passes.
When finished, summarize: files changed, why those changes, and what is left undone.
goal.write:
Write a {genre} about {topic} for {reader}.
Must land one point: {claim}; tone: {tone}; length: {length}; every claim needs a source link.
Outline first — I will confirm before you draft the body.
goal.research:
Research {target} to answer {question}.
Every conclusion needs a source (link or file path); separate verified fact from inference; cover {range}; end with 3 actionable next steps.
No file edits needed — get the answer right first.

cmd.office1: Summarize this down to 300 words: keep every number and conclusion
cmd.office2: Find factual errors, inconsistent metrics and open questions in this draft
cmd.office3: Rewrite it for {audience} — do not modify the original files
cmd.dev1: Run /plan first — wait for my confirmation before changing anything
cmd.dev2: Find the root cause of this error; propose the smallest fix; no opportunistic refactoring
cmd.dev3: Run {verify} and group the failures by root cause
cmd.write1: Give three headline directions, each with a one-line claim
cmd.write2: Draft the opening paragraph from that outline — I want to set the tone first
cmd.write3: Rewrite this in a {tone} voice; change no facts
cmd.research1: List the three key assumptions first, then find evidence for each
cmd.research2: Split the findings into three columns: verified fact / inference / needs checking
cmd.research3: Give three next steps, each with its cost and risk
